name: Human Virology
description: Introduction, overview and history of medical virology; virus genetics and molecular methods in virology. Virus structure, classification, symmetries and replication; principles of viral pathogenesis, clearance and persistence; respiratory viruses -influenza, paramyxoviruses, SARS; viral gastroenteritis - causative agents, epidemiology; hepatitis viruses; infections in immunocompromised individuals, latency; enteroviruses – polio, ECHO, coxsackie viruses; congenital viral infections, prevention; retroviruses – HIV, AIDS; arboviruses, viral zoonoses – arthropod vectors, urban and sylvatic transmission cycles, rabies and viral haemorrhagic fevers; tumour viruses- oncogenic mechanisms of viruses; strategies for control of viral infection – active and passive immunoprophylaxis, antiviral agents; case studies from literature, evolving and emerging areas of interest.
